source_excerpts.text:
## 2. A complete theorem for commuting correlated dephasing

### The model

There are \(m\) finite-dimensional parties, with one nonconstant local Hermitian observable \(A_i\) per party. Let

\[
U=U^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{m\times m},
\qquad
C=R+iJ\succeq0,
\]

where \(R=R^{\mathsf T}\) is real and \(J=-J^{\mathsf T}\) is real. Consider

\[
\mathcal L(\rho)=
-i\left[\frac12\sum_{ij}U_{ij}A_iA_j,\rho\right]
+
\sum_{ij}C_{ij}
\left(
A_i\rho A_j-\frac12\{A_iA_j,\rho\}
\right).
\]

This includes commuting bilinear interactions and arbitrary correlated Markovian dephasing within the stated operator family. Commuting local Hamiltonians can also be included.

Here, “classical mediation” means local operations and classical communication, without a pre-existing shared entangled resource.

### The criterion

The semigroup \(e^{t\mathcal L}\) preserves every fully separable input for every \(t\ge0\) **if and only if** there are real diagonal matrices \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d)\) and \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s)\) such that

\[
\boxed{
\Sigma(D,s)=
\begin{pmatrix}
D &-\frac12(U+S+J)\\[2mm]
-\frac12(U+S-J)&R-D
\end{pmatrix}
\succeq0 .
}
\]

This has three consequences.

1. **It gives an exact structural decision problem.** There is one \(2m\times2m\) positive-semidefinite constraint with \(2m\) real diagonal variables. Strict feasibility or infeasibility margins can be verified with rational certificates.

2. **Feasibility supplies a physical implementation.** The channel at any finite time is implemented by local Gaussian-pointer measurements, classical communication and local phase feedback.

3. **Infeasibility supplies an experiment.** A product of local two-eigenlevel superpositions becomes non-fully-separable at every sufficiently small positive time. A dual certificate supplies a two-body witness, and a second-derivative bound supplies a certified finite time at which its expectation is negative.

The formulation is polynomial in matrix size. It is not a claim of exact polynomial-bit decision arbitrarily close to an ill-conditioned boundary.

7. What this adds over the strongest applicable approaches

The comparisons materially constrain the claim.

Existing machinery	What it already supplies	Established addition here
Astra N1201	A positive Gaussian finite-time instrument and correct outcome-weighted simulation	Necessity derived from all separable decompositions, completing the classification for the stated general correlated-noise model
Dephasing partial-transpose criteria	Powerful entangling conditions and negativity diagnostics	An explicit purely dissipative all-PPT entangling example, plus the complete full-separability boundary
Covariance and local-uncertainty SDPs	Strong witnesses, including detection beyond partial transpose	A proof that a particular covariance condition is complete for this dynamical class
Readout averaging and mitigation	Symmetrization and calibrated correction of readout effects	A null-preserving use of private controls that requires no detector inversion
Measurement-device-independent witnesses	Certification with trusted quantum inputs under their device contracts	A different contract using trusted local controls and an unknown joint POVM; no general dominance claim
Exact noisy-Ising correlator methods	Efficient evaluation of many observables in this model family	Structural classification and operational certification, without a claimed simulation speedup

The covariance comparison is especially important: the strongest matched covariance SDP, given the same acquired moments, can produce the same kind of witness. I have not established a better estimator. Covariance criteria were already developed as powerful separability tests, and exact noisy-Ising correlation methods already avoid full density-matrix simulation for many observables.
